analysis: The 9am story is the intraday reversal, not the morning rally: the post-jobs bond bid faded fast, with the 10Y snapping back from ~5.16% to ~5.25% and the 2Y to 4.82%, cutting the Dow's gain from +400 to +121 points (+0.2%) while the Nasdaq still held a new all-time high at +1.1-1.2%. The signal is that the dovish payrolls print (29k vs ~84-90k expected, unemployment 4.2%) did real work on the Fed path — October hike odds fell to ~19-21% from ~64-69% a week ago — but one soft print could not hold bond prices down against a still-hawkish speaker slate (Logan's +50bp call Thursday; Logan and August factory orders due later today). Leadership is still AI-infrastructure, now spreading from semis breakouts (NVDA, UMC, TER) into server/storage names (HPE +7% through its 63.44 buy point, NetApp +5% for an eighth straight session). Tesla is the day's cleanest held beat: +5.7% to ~$367, no repeat of Q2's sell-the-news, and Barron's 'new EV race' frame is grounded — GM EV sales -60%+, Ford -80%, Rivian +46%. Noise to discount: the yield snapback chatter and the G7/EU 100M-barrel headline — a proposal being talked about, not a decided release, with OPEC+ meeting Sunday. The two carried single-source AI stories (Amazon's $8B Nvidia-chip SPV, Broadcom's $60B Anthropic financing) remain the unconfirmed swing factors. Breadth is still the weak spot from Thursday's data (only 49% of the S&P above its 200-day; ~222 of 503 advancing into a +0.6% index).
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Bond-yield snapback took a chunk out of the morning rally: the 10Y rebounded from ~5.16% to ~5.25%, the 2Y back to 4.82% and the 30Y to 5.61%, with the Dow paring from +400 to +121 points (+0.2%), the S&P 500 +0.7% and the Nasdaq +1.1-1.2%. The Nasdaq still touched a new all-time high (Investopedia).
headlines.why_it_matters: The key intraday tell — the dovish repricing held on the Fed path (October hike odds ~19-21% vs ~64-69% a week ago) but one soft print could not keep bonds bid; growth held up better than value into the fade.

headlines.headline: Tesla held the Q3-deliveries beat into the morning, +5.7% to ~$366.78-367.66, with 486,532 deliveries vs 456,896-461,974 estimates; the Q2 beat-then--7.5% template did not repeat. Barron's framed it as Tesla winning the 'new EV race' as legacy EVs fade: GM EV sales fell 60%+ to ~25,000 units, Ford EV sales dropped 80%, while Rivian deliveries rose 46% YoY to 19,248. Energy storage missed at 13.7 vs 15.9 GWh expected; Q3 earnings due Oct 21.
headlines.why_it_matters: A held beat with industry-share confirmation — competitors' EV lines are collapsing while Tesla's stabilized, so the print reads as demand share gain, not a one-off; the energy miss and Q4's 311,448-unit hurdle are the offsets.

headlines.headline: AI-infrastructure breadth extended beyond semis: HPE jumped 7% through its 63.44 buy point and NetApp rallied 5%, poised for an eighth straight winning session — both among the day's top S&P 500 gainers.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI bid is spreading from chip names (NVDA's 234.76 breakout, UMC, TER +7%) into server and storage — broader leadership legs than a pure rate-repricing rally.

headlines.headline: WTI crude sold off 2.5% to ~$90.50 (Brent back under $100) on reports of a G7/EU coordinated ~100M-barrel crude-and-diesel stock release; the US is pressing Europe to act on spiking diesel prices, with reports of a potential US diesel export ban if Europe does not. OPEC+ meets Sunday.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rates-friendly on paper via cheaper energy, but this is proposal-stage, not a decided release — headline-sensitive for oil; an OPEC+ pushback or no decision Sunday reverses it.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: Meta faces a fresh legal overhang as New Mexico reportedly seeks up to $40 billion in data-privacy penalties stemming from the Cambridge Analytica case.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile; a headline-size penalty number is the kind of item that moves a megacap on confirmation, so watch for official confirmation rather than trading the first report.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: Nike is still down ~9% after the Q1 miss ($11.21B revenue vs ~$11.32B consensus), a 26% Greater China decline and soft FY27 guidance with restructuring-linked job cuts; the FT's Amazon-$8B-Nvidia-chip story and Bloomberg's Broadcom-$60B-Anthropic-financing story remain single-source and unresolved.
headlines.why_it_matters: Nike is the real consumer-demand counterweight to the dovish macro; the two AI-finance stories are the unresolved single-source swing factors for the AI trade.

Underlying breadth still the weak spot (8am: only 49% of S&P above 200-day; Thursday only ~222 of 503 advancing into a +0.6% index). S&P set for a ~1% weekly decline even after today's bounce. Zacks raised its Q3 2026 EPS estimate to $0.21 (from $0.20) on Oct 1, Hold rating; FY2026 consensus $1.17; Q2 beat ($0.31 vs $0.28) on $342.15M revenue; $600M private placement of 6.75% senior notes due 2035. Later today: August factory orders data plus comments from Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan (said Thursday rates may need +50bp) — first post-print Fed read.
Confirmation or denial of the FT Amazon-$8B-chip and Bloomberg Broadcom-$60B-Anthropic stories; and any official confirmation on the Meta/New Mexico $40B penalty report.
